fixtures.studentAnswer: Given triangles ABC and DEF with AB=DE, BC=EF and CA=FD, we have all three corresponding sides equal. Therefore by the SSS congruence condition the triangles are congruent.

expected.feedback: Excellent work – you stated the triangles, chose the correct SSS rule, matched corresponding sides and concluded congruence.

fixtures.studentAnswer: Triangles PQR and XYZ have PQ=XY and QR=YZ and angle Q equals angle Y, so by SAS they are congruent and hence ΔPQR ≅ ΔXYZ.

expected.feedback: You correctly used the SAS criterion to show the triangles are congruent.

fixtures.studentAnswer: Consider ΔABC and ΔDEF. We have AB=DE and BC=EF. Also angle A equals angle D. Therefore the triangles are similar by AA and hence congruent.

expected.feedback: You listed some equal parts but invoked a similarity rule (AA) instead of a valid congruence rule and did not properly conclude congruence.

fixtures.studentAnswer: Triangles ABC and DEF are proven congruent because their corresponding angles are equal (AAA). Since AAA shows similarity, the triangles must also be congruent.

expected.feedback: AAA only proves similarity; it does not guarantee congruence. State the triangles and use one of SSS/SAS/ASA/RHS to prove congruence.

fixtures.studentAnswer: In right triangles ABC and DEF, the hypotenuse AC equals DF and one leg AB equals DE. Therefore by the RHS criterion the triangles are congruent.

expected.feedback: Correct application of the RHS (right‑angle hypotenuse side) criterion.

fixtures.studentAnswer: Given ΔABC and ΔDEF, angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E. Two equal angles imply ΔABC ~ ΔDEF by the AA similarity criterion, hence the ratios of corresponding sides are proportional and the triangles are similar.

expected.feedback: You correctly used the AA criterion and concluded similarity with proportional sides.

fixtures.studentAnswer: Triangles PQR and XYZ have PQ=XY, QR=YZ and angle Q equals angle Y. Therefore the triangles are similar by SAS.

expected.feedback: You invoked SAS similarity but did not explicitly compare the ratio of corresponding sides. Show the proportionality of sides to complete the proof.

fixtures.studentAnswer: Triangles ABC and DEF are similar because all three sides are equal (AB=DE, BC=EF, CA=FD). Therefore ΔABC ≅ ΔDEF.

expected.feedback: Listing equal sides without establishing proportional ratios does not satisfy SSS similarity. Also, you concluded congruence instead of similarity.

fixtures.studentAnswer: In triangle ABC, D and E are midpoints of AB and AC respectively. Since DE is parallel to BC, by the basic proportionality theorem we have AD/DB = AE/EC and hence the segments are proportional.

expected.feedback: You correctly identified the midpoints, stated the basic proportionality theorem and set up the ratio.

fixtures.studentAnswer: In triangle ABC, D is the midpoint of AB. Therefore AD = DB, so the triangle is isosceles.

expected.feedback: You identified a midpoint but did not state the basic proportionality theorem or set up a proportional ratio.

fixtures.studentAnswer: In triangle ABC with DE parallel to BC, the ratio AD/AB equals AE/AC.

expected.feedback: The ratio should involve segments on the same sides (AD/DB = AE/EC). Ensure you set up the correct proportionality.

fixtures.studentAnswer: In triangle ABC, AD bisects angle A. According to the angle bisector theorem, BD/DC = AB/AC, so the sides are divided proportionally.

expected.feedback: You clearly identified the angle bisector, stated the theorem and set up the correct ratio.

fixtures.studentAnswer: In triangle ABC, the bisector of angle A divides BC into segments BD and DC so that BD = DC.

expected.feedback: The angle bisector theorem relates the ratio of adjacent sides to the segments on the opposite side; it does not assert BD = DC.

fixtures.studentAnswer: In triangle ABC with bisector AD, the theorem gives AB/BC = BD/DC.

expected.feedback: The correct ratio is BD/DC = AB/AC; ensure you relate the segments adjacent to the bisected angle.

fixtures.studentAnswer: Given triangles ABC and DEF where AB = DE, BC = EF and angle B = angle E, to prove the triangles are congruent. From the given data we know two sides and the included angle are equal, so by SAS the triangles are congruent.

expected.feedback: You clearly stated the given information, what to prove, matched the equal parts and applied the SAS criterion to conclude congruence.
